title: The Modest Husband and His Devoted Wife

keywords: tale of the ugly man and his beautiful wife
full_text:
In Baghdad lived a humble artisan named Abu Bakr, who was born with a face so plain and scarred by childhood illness that people often turned their heads in the street. Yet his wife, Layla, was celebrated across the quarter for her extraordinary beauty and noble grace.

Curious neighbors often asked Layla in secret: 'How can a maiden of your peerless beauty live in such radiant joy with a husband so plain?'

Layla smiled with deep, soulful wisdom and answered:

'You look upon my husband’s face, but you do not see his heart. In thirty years, he has never spoken an unkind word; when I am weary, he carries the water; when I am sick, he watches by my bed like an angel of mercy; his hands are pure, his speech is gentle, and his fidelity is as steadfast as the mountains.

Outward beauty is a blossom that fades in a single season of fever or age; but a noble character, a loving heart, and an upright soul grow more beautiful with every passing year.

I look into his eyes, and I see the truest, handsomest man in all Baghdad.'

Her words spread through the city, teaching all who heard them that true love is built on the enduring beauty of the soul, which time cannot tarnish.
moral: Inner character, kindness, and devotion shine brighter than any fleeting physical beauty.
